Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for taking time to engage on our procurement checklist. A few follow-ups from the SRE and vendor security teams — can you provide concise answers to the items below so we can progress to legal and finance? We need concrete details to bake into our MSA and SLO exhibit.

1) Uptime/SLO commitments: what is the standard availability SLO (monthly/rolling) for the Redwood hosted inference API? Any tiered SLAs (enterprise/dedicated)? How do you measure availability (ingress success vs end-to-end token completion)?
2) Latency SLOs: do you publish p50/p95/p99 latency targets by model class? What measurement window and percentile definitions are used?
3) Monitoring & metrics: what metrics will you expose to customers (names & units preferred), how often are they updated, and how long are they retained?
4) Customer access: do customers get read-only dashboards (Grafana) or raw metrics export? What auth/SSO options exist?
5) Alerting & escalation: how are SLO breaches detected & alerted, who is on-call, and what are the escalation contacts/response times?
6) Exceptions & credits: process for SLA exceptions, measurement disputes, and credit calculation examples.

We appreciate short, bullet answers; we may follow up for clarifications. If possible we’d like a read-only dashboard link or a short demo next week.

Thanks,

Hi Tom,

Appreciate the clear list — answers below are high level; I’ve attached the SLO baseline doc and a short guide for Grafana read-only access. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through dashboards next week.

1) Uptime/SLO commitments:
- Hosted API (standard plan): 99.5% monthly availability (measured as successful API responses / total requests, 5xx counted as failures).
- Enterprise (Dedicated/Reserved): 99.95% monthly availability with SLA credits and a named escalation path.
- Measurement is at the API layer (ingress -> final model completion) to reflect customer-observed availability.

2) Latency SLOs:
- We publish p50/p95 for inference time per model class in the catalog. Typical targets: small models p95 < 200ms, medium p95 < 400ms, large p95 < 800ms (region and seq len dependent).
- Percentiles are computed on rolling 30-day windows by default; alerting can be configured on 24h or 7d windows.

3) Monitoring & metrics:
- Exposed metrics: request_success_rate (ratio), p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, token_throughput_rps, cpu_util_percent, gpu_util_percent, kv_cache_hit_rate.
- Granularity: 1m for system metrics, 10s aggregated for request/latency metrics where feasible.
- Retention: metrics retained 90 days by default; enterprise plans can extend to 365 days for aggregated metrics and 1 year for logs/audit trails.

4) Customer access:
- Customers receive read-only Grafana dashboards (SSO via SAML/OIDC) plus a Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint (read-only ingest). Raw model internal state (KV cache contents, model weights) is never exportable.
- We can provide scheduled CSV exports for aggregated metrics on request.

5) Alerting & escalation:
- SLO breaches are detected by our monitoring pipeline (rolling windows). Default alerts: SLO degradation (P95 latency > target for >15m), availability drops (success_rate < threshold for >5m).
- Alerts route to our SRE team, with enterprise customers getting a named on-call and phone escalation. Response SLA: initial ack within 30 minutes for Sev 1.

6) Exceptions & credits:
- Exceptions: customers request an exception via support ticket + review with account team; temporary adjustments are negotiable for scheduled maintenance or capacity migrations.
- Credits: calculated monthly as a percentage of the monthly invoice per the attached SLA credit matrix. Example in attached XLSX.

Attachments: Redwood_SLO_Baseline_2025.pdf, Grafana-ReadOnly-Guide.md, SLA-Credit-Matrix.xlsx

If helpful I can include Karthik (sales) and Evelyn (security) on the thread to confirm the enterprise-level details and SSO setup. When are you available for the demo?

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa / Karthik — quick bullets from security/compliance side: we can offer the following to Acme under enterprise contract: 

- Read-only Grafana dashboards: Yes — SAML-based SSO with RBAC. Customers get a pre-provisioned organisation and read-only role; we do not allow editing dashboards or creating new datasource queries.
- Metrics & names allowed: the list Marissa provided is fine (request_success_rate, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, token_throughput_rps, cpu_util_percent, gpu_util_percent, kv_cache_hit_rate). No raw KV cache dumps or model weight access.
- Retention: metrics (1m/10s resolution) retained 90 days by default; aggregated retention up to 365 days on enterprise. Logs and audit trails retained 1 year when contracted.
- Measurement details: SLOs measured at the API surface; success defined as 2xx response and token stream complete within timeout. Latency percentile windows computed across completed requests only.
- Alerting & escalations: default routing to platform SRE Slack + PagerDuty. For enterprise we provide a named on-call with phone and escalation matrix.
- Measurement disputes: we provide the raw time-series for the contested window to reconcile; disputes must be raised within 30 days of the invoice period.

Security caveat: we cannot expose request payloads or any content that would reveal customer prompts or outputs. Any metric that could be reverse-engineered to reconstruct customer data is redacted.

If they want longer retention or export of aggregated metrics we should add it to the SOW/price list.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
